newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices rise on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices rise on weather.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Midwest were trading higher Monday as a cold weather front moved through the area over the weekend boosting power demand for heating, industry sources said.
Cold weather was expected to dominate through most of the week, with heavy snow reported in northeast Ohio.
Trade was said to be relatively thin, with some utilities shut to honor Veterans Day.
"It was quiet, but it is cold in lots of these areas and I think people are thinking that tomorrow is going to be even worse so prices moved higher," said one Mid-West trader.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday delivery rose to $27.00-29.00 from a range $23.00-28.00 late last week, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power were said to be little changed in thin trade at $12.50-14.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
December peak ECAR was talked higher in the $19.60-19.90 range from near $19.50 late last week, while January/February ECAR was assessed at $21.60-21.95 per MWh.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were talked as high as $30.00 from a range of $18.00-20.00 late last week, although trade was said to be near non-existant due to line-loading in the region.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices were notionally assessed steady in the $8.50-10.00 area.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), the cold weather pushed next day non-firm peak power prices to $29.00-34.00 from $19.50-22.25 late last week, the traders said.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Tuesday delivery were talked stronger at $27.00-31.00 per MWh from $22.00-25.25 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak SPP was pegged at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
December SPP was assessed in the $21.75-22.05 range, the brokers and marketers said.
